note: A shrunk counterexample of the fuzz suite's inversions, kept on 2026-10-08 with ves-bessel-tables-578342b9.json. A Schlumberger sounding of 3.2 ohm-m with a reading of 5.1 ohm-m at the first spacing. The two engines stopped at the same model to 6e-4 (a top layer of 38,261 ohm-m in the browser and 38,239 in Python, 0.204 m thick) and reported fits of 0.5561 and 0.5608 percent: Python's forward model gives 0.5612 at the browser's own model, so the difference was the forward model, not the search. The browser built its quadrature tables from Numerical Recipes' J0 and J1, good to 5e-9. Under a thin resistive top layer the forward model is the top layer's resistivity plus an integral that cancels nearly all of it, so that error reached the apparent resistivity multiplied by rho1 / rho_a: 1.5e-4 at 10,000 ohm-m and 1.5e-3 at 100,000 over a few ohm-m (reference.json's ves_forward grid). The browser now builds its tables from Cephes j0 and j1, as scipy does, and the fits agree. Perturbing Python's forward model by 1e-15 to 1e-10 in four shapes (a cosine and a sine in the log of the spacing, a ramp in it, and a uniform scaling) moves its own answer by at most 1.9e-7, inside parity's 1e-3.
